resolutions: The construction selects restricted-use or general-use shape; the user does not choose that shape separately.
Noun class is lexical authority. Visible spelling limits candidates but never invents class membership.
Subject number and stem-internal affinity or distributive meaning remain separate grammatical dimensions.
Class and typed lexical alternatives select number connectors; the connector is not a noun suffix.
Possessive singular or common forms use only the class-authorized base or truncated general-use stem.
Truncation deletes only a typed ephemeral final a or i and never performs blind string deletion.
Supportive i repairs only a licensed Subclass 2-C cluster and spelling rules apply after that repair.
A visible final uh, tl, tli, o, or m never selects its own constituent analysis.
Typed alternatives remain open until a user or external lexical authority selects one; spelling alone is never authority.
Vowel length and supportive-i boundary behavior remain explicit even where traditional spelling hides them.
